report_html:
Bleed the Clock

The backfield runs through one man — their top back absorbs 66% of the carries (league ~59%), a true bell-cow share that makes his rushing volume among the safest floors in the sport when the script cooperates.

The Offensive Blueprint

They're a heavy under-center team (58% shotgun vs ~68%) — a pro-style, run-committed structure.

They run downhill — mostly inside the tackles (20% to the edge vs ~25%), a gap/power scheme that trades big plays for a steady, grinding floor.

By the numbers it's an efficient unit — a 48% success rate (above the 44% average).

In the Red Zone

Their red-zone identity is run-first (42% pass), funnelling touchdown equity to the lead back.

Defense — Soft on the Ground

They surrender 126 rushing and 209 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). The run moves against them — target opposing RB1s.

They lock down opposing tight ends — just 24 rec yds/game (vs ~35); fade receiving props there.

They lock down opposing WR2s — just 28 rec yds/game (vs ~36); fade receiving props there.

Soft against opposing WR1s — 64 rec yds/game (vs ~58). A rec-yards target.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: back their RB1's rushing volume in favored/positive scripts; opposing RB1s smash on the ground and at the goal line.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
